purpose: Test whether the overseas industrial field-service residual is one isolated exporter case or a repeated Xuzhou OEM demand pattern with independently hungry local-service supply.

observed_named_actors.actor: 松谷激光科技（江苏）有限公司
observed_named_actors.evidence: Current Xuzhou/Suining overseas after-sales engineer role requires customer-site installation, training, process commissioning and fault troubleshooting; US visa preferred.

observed_named_actors.actor: 中航迈特增材制造（徐州）有限公司 / 中航迈特
observed_named_actors.evidence: Current overseas after-sales role handles overseas 3D-printer installation/commissioning/training/service and requires overseas travel; company is simultaneously expanding overseas sales/channel capability.

observed_named_actors.actor: 徐州徐工矿业机械有限公司 / 徐工集团
observed_named_actors.evidence: Current overseas-service roles cover overseas maintenance, operation training, field support and short overseas debugging support.

observed_named_actors.actor: 徐州鹏程电气有限公司
observed_named_actors.evidence: Recent Kenya exhibition created a concrete follow-up local operating-condition test after an EPC measured equipment interfaces.

demand_cluster.interpretation: Cross-border OEM engineer dispatch is a repeated observable operating pattern in Xuzhou equipment manufacturing, not a single-company hypothetical need.

observed_named_actors.evidence: Industrial field-service provider publicly markets local execution for machine builders/OEMs and a Shanghai-based business-development signal explicitly seeks a first strategic Chinese equipment-company customer.

Markets on-ground commissioning/training/breakdown response specifically to Chinese OEMs; publicly claims existing work for a Chinese casting-equipment OEM and quotes local service from about USD 250/day.
Offers outsourced/whitelabel installation, commissioning and ongoing field service to machine builders/OEMs under OEM documentation and acceptance criteria.

Field-service marketplaces demonstrate global contractor routing, work-order approval and payments, but are materially stronger in IT/networking/generic field service than OEM-specific industrial machinery commissioning.

supply_cluster.interpretation: Supply-side willingness and execution capability are real; generic local-engineer availability is not the missing edge.

adjacent_objective_evidence: 宇晶股份 public financing material states overseas technical support/after-sales currently relies mainly on domestic remote guidance or temporary dispatched staff; response efficiency is low and the company plans local service teams.

A current Wuxi industrial-automation overseas-engineer role explicitly splits work: outsourced providers perform positioning/installation/basic commissioning while HQ technicians support precision commissioning and qualification.
ServiceNow now has a Field Service Marketplace for pushing work-order tasks to eligible contractors, confirming that contractor-marketplace mechanics themselves are mature.
observed_partial_flow: OEMs hire and dispatch their own overseas service engineers.
OEMs use agents/EPCs/local contractors for selected lower-level tasks.
Local industrial service providers seek OEM work and can operate under OEM documentation/acceptance.
Contractor marketplaces already route generic field-service tasks.
strongest_counterevidence: Klose already offers whitelabel field service under OEM acceptance criteria across multiple regions.
Mehnert is directly trying to acquire Chinese equipment makers, which can remove the need for an intermediary.
Naleno/MyMobiForce/ServiceNow show contractor routing, approval and payment are not novel mechanics.
Large OEMs such as XCMG and mature brands can build their own local networks.

售意达/售后宝 and enterprise FSM products already manage overseas work orders, SOPs, external service providers, evidence, acceptance, settlement and global service records; software workflow/control-plane mechanics alone are market-served.
candidate.narrowed_missing_edge_hypothesis: The surviving possible gap is not technician search and not aftermarket/FSM software. It is accountable execution supply: a China-side multi-country service layer for smaller/mid-sized equipment OEMs that has real qualified local industrial providers behind the work order, can substitute providers after failure, and owns provider qualification + execution evidence + acceptance continuity across countries while the OEM retains technical/warranty authority.

rooter_execution_map.demand_actor: Xuzhou/Jiangsu equipment OEM with intermittent overseas onsite work that does not justify owned service staff in every destination
rooter_execution_map.supply_actor: country-specific industrial field-service providers and licensed technicians
rooter_execution_map.partial_flow: OEM travel + agents/EPCs + direct local contractors + outsourced field-service providers already coexist
rooter_execution_map.missing_edge: UNPROVEN: after agents/EPCs and existing FSM software exist, whether OEMs still lack reliable, replaceable local industrial execution capacity with one accountable interface for provider qualification, field evidence, acceptance and replacement.
rooter_execution_map.task_unit: one OEM-defined installation / survey / SAT / commissioning-support / diagnosis / maintenance work order
rooter_execution_map.acceptance: OEM SOP + qualification check + evidence package + measurements/test data + customer/OEM signoff
rooter_execution_map.payer: OEM or contractually responsible overseas buyer
rooter_execution_map.money_flow: payer -> orchestration/control-plane layer -> local service provider
rooter_execution_map.operator_role: China-side intake, task schema, provider graph, qualification, routing, remote expert coordination, evidence/acceptance, settlement and cross-job performance data
rooter_execution_map.operator_non_role: not the onsite engineer; not a visa/travel agency; not generic lead generation; not the party assuming unlicensed technical liability
rooter_execution_map.exit_path: repeatable OEM task templates + multi-provider graph + acceptance/reputation data + delegated operations

reachability.demand_side: A/B for several Xuzhou/Jiangsu actors via public recruiting/company channels
reachability.supply_side: C currently; public online contacts exist but providers are outside Jiangsu/overseas

mobilization.explanation: Bilateral pull is now materially stronger and economic spread is plausible, but demand self-propulsion and willingness to pay a separate orchestration layer remain unproven. Founder-led OEM sales would currently still be required.

kill_conditions: Named Xuzhou OEMs say overseas service travel is normal/acceptable and local partner management is not a material recurring cost.
OEMs can directly contract one existing provider such as Klose/Mehnert/country partner with little search, qualification or acceptance friction.
The proposed value collapses to referral/lead generation and can be bypassed after one introduction.
Each task is too OEM-specific to standardize enough for provider substitution or operator exit.
Liability/warranty/IP rules require the OEM's own employee for most commercially important tasks.
Existing FSM software plus the OEM's current agent/service-provider pool already gives reliable execution, replacement and accountability; only software setup/configuration remains.
promotion_conditions: At least one named Xuzhou/Jiangsu OEM confirms a recent overseas work order where existing agent/provider management still caused measurable travel, delay, downtime, acceptance or coordination cost.
The OEM would prefer one China-side accountable interface across more than one destination/provider rather than separately sourcing each local firm.
At least two independent local providers accept OEM-defined SOP/evidence/white-label or equivalent execution terms.
A bounded work order has clear provider payout and a credible separate orchestration margin.
Demand can originate from a recurring channel or installed-base workflow rather than founder cold-selling every job.

portfolio_effect.oms_005a_pengcheng_kenya: Retained as one concrete sensor case under the broader cluster candidate, not independently promoted.
portfolio_effect.current_best_next_truth: Resolve the execution-supply question, not the software question: after agents/EPCs and FSM/work-order systems already exist, does a named Xuzhou/Jiangsu OEM still fail to obtain reliable, replaceable local industrial execution for a bounded task, with measurable travel/delay/downtime/acceptance cost?
portfolio_effect.next_public_search: Look for named equipment OEM disclosures/cases where local-service outsourcing exists but cross-provider quality, qualification, acceptance, warranty or accountability remains costly; prefer Xuzhou/Jiangsu.
